_schema_source: edit_captions action=template with no templatePreset, 2026-09-22, catalog=all. The KEY NAMES BELOW ARE THEIRS, read from that response — not guessed. 26 presets came back, not 27; if a 27th exists it is outside the 'all' catalog and the count should be re-read rather than reconciled by hand.
_styleProfile_excludes: Their own message: 'Style profiles exclude font size, position, and visual row capacity.' So our fontSize and position values are NOT styleProfile fields and must not be merged in as if they were — size goes through the track style as sizePx (stored as fontSizeRatio = sizePx / min(w,h)), position through layout/anchor. Our maxWordsPerLine is a THIRD profile: paginationProfile.wordsPerPage.
_merge_rule: action=style MERGES, it does not replace. Each profile below names the built-in it should be applied OVER — template <preset> first, then style — chosen as the nearest of the 26 so the merge has the least to override. B1's first Gadzhi frame carried a purple box from an earlier probe, which is what a merge onto whatever was there last looks like.
_THE_HIGHLIGHT_FINDING: THEIR HIGHLIGHT IS TEMPORAL AND OURS WAS LEXICAL, and THEIRS IS WHAT SHIPS (Zac, 2026-09-22). hasActiveHighlight + highlightUnit 'word' lights the word being SPOKEN, walking the line with the playhead; Gadzhi, Lumen and Pulse lit a word from a fixed keyword list. There is no keyword concept in styleProfile. The three LINES were rewritten to describe the spoken-word highlight, because a line that still said 'one keyword lit' would be describing a render nobody will ever see — and whatever is not in the line their AI invents.

_NOT_EXPRESSIBLE.Prime: line1Color/line2Color — styleProfile has ONE `color`, no per-line colour.
_NOT_EXPRESSIBLE.TwoTone: topColor/accentColor — same gap: the second line's accent has no key.
_NOT_EXPRESSIBLE._consequence: Both render as a single-colour line unless B1's schema has a per-line key the catalog response does not show. Stated rather than mapped onto highlightColor, which would paint the wrong thing and look deliberate.

CleanCut._line: CleanCut — plain white words for narration, explainers and text that must not steal focus
CleanCut._why: Inter, #ffffff, highlight-off, no background, no stroke — only weight and shadow differ.

Cove._line: Cove — words that appear one at a time as they are spoken for narration and demos
Cove._why: No background and no highlight in its DEFAULT state — the box and serif belong to boxedWords, which defaults to empty. plain is the least to override.
Cove._depends_on: per-word reveal from token times — unspoken words are opacity 0
Cove._not_expressible: boxedWords (Playfair italic at 1.8x with a dot) is unreachable — it needs a word list, and there is no word-list concept. Default Cove has none set, so nothing is lost today.

Gadzhi._line: Gadzhi — uppercase words with the spoken one lit in yellow for punchlines and key terms
Gadzhi._why: uppercase + highlight-word + shadow + no background + no stroke is Gadzhi's exact structure; Story Yellow adds a stroke and a highlight block it does not have.
Gadzhi._not_expressible: Our keyword highlight was LEXICAL — a fixed word list. dogme's is TEMPORAL and that is what ships: the yellow walks the line with the playhead. The line was rewritten to say so rather than left describing a keyword.

Lumen._line: Lumen — soft white words with the spoken one in amber for hype, reveals and energy
Lumen._why: highlight-word + shadow + NO background + no stroke + no uppercase. Corrected off `studio`: studio carries a normalBackground and LUMEN HAS NO BACKGROUND AT ALL — `bandLuma` is a MEASUREMENT of the video behind the caption, fed to keywordContrastShadow to step contrast up, not a band that gets painted. I had read a measured input as a drawn element.
Lumen._not_expressible: The keyword also changes FACE (Playfair Display 400 italic) and SIZE (1.3x), and a shine word goes to 1.6x with a sweep. styleProfile varies COLOUR per word and nothing else, so the face swap and the shine do not travel. Stated rather than approximated with a second colour.

Prime._line: Prime — two stacked lines in white and blue for setups, payoffs and question-answer beats
Prime._why: Inter, no background, no stroke, single display mode. Its two lines are ordinary wrapping at 3 words, NOT their stacked mode.
Prime._not_expressible: line1Color #FFFFFF / line2Color #3BA5FF — styleProfile has ONE `color` and no per-line key, so both lines ship white. Mapping the blue onto highlightColor would light the SPOKEN word blue, which is a different thing that looks deliberate.

Pulse._line: Pulse — clean words with the spoken one in coral for calm delivery and slow reveals
Pulse._why: Story Yellow is already DM Sans with highlight-word and a shadow — the same family as ours, so only the weight, the highlight colour and the 1px stroke need overriding.
Pulse._not_expressible: The keyword is also 1.25x with a glow off the highlight colour. No per-word scale key, so it ships as colour alone.

TwoTone._line: TwoTone — bold uppercase white words with a thick dark outline for loud punchy beats
TwoTone._why: White + a real stroke + shadow + highlight-off + no background, which is TwoTone's whole structure. ITS OUTLINE IS UNIFORM, not per-word — every word carries the same 6px stroke — so it is NOT highlight-bearing and does not wait on the diff.
TwoTone._not_expressible: line 2 in accentColor #FFC53D has no per-line key in styleProfile, so ChatCut renders every line white. THE LINE WAS REWRITTEN TO MATCH WHAT RENDERS rather than what our component does: 'the second in a warm accent' was true of the Remotion body and false of the preset, which is the half B1 caught.

_status: FIVE PRESETS LIVE: CleanCut, Cove, Gadzhi, Pulse, TwoTone. Prime and Lumen cut 2026-09-23 — their identity does not survive the mapping into styleProfile.
_single_source: THIS FILE IS THE ONLY SOURCE FOR ALL SEVEN — baseline, style, size, layout, pagination, line, and the not-expressible notes. B1 builds from it and nothing else.
